active_task.goal: Synchronize Settings configuration and version-audit column heights and scrollbar styling

warm_memory.summary: Phase 50 fixes Settings integration-page column synchronization. The left configuration surface now determines the desktop grid-row height, while the audit panel fills that height without contributing long diff payloads to intrinsic sizing. Version and diff regions scroll internally with the global light-console scrollbar treatment. All five audit-enabled integration pages have a measured 0px left/right height delta; the stacked breakpoint remains bounded and overflow-safe.
constraints: Do not revive the rejected visible decision-queue surface
Do not revive the visible delivery cockpit unless the product value is redefined
Keep runtime/generated `task_status.md` and `well-ambient.db` changes out of source commits unless explicitly requested
Use `ui-skill` by default for frontend UI changes, falling back to `finesse-skill` then `taste-skill`
Do not remount the project health telemetry panel unless its operator workflow is redefined
Jira Task is the demand mainline in this deployment; execution subtasks are supporting evidence
Continue the UI redesign by routing real modules through the new shell while avoiding broad rewrites of legacy business panels
Browser visual verification currently requires a real login; do not attempt browser policy workarounds
decisions: Treat the Phase 41 redesign as product UI: SPECTACLE=2, DENSITY=8, light management workspace, table-first, inspector-backed, and evidence-first.
Add the coded prototype before full migration because existing Svelte pages are large and business-critical.
Gate the prototype behind `config:read` rather than replacing decision/schedule/evidence/settings pages.
Keep the prototype centered on exception, schedule, evidence, and override workflows, not a generic queue or broad cockpit.
Use the Phase 41 token substrate and `contract.ts` shapes as the foundation for production page migration.
Use a table-first command surface and right-side inspector as the core production-page interaction.
Use grouped submenus when a page has multiple configuration/security subareas, but render those submenus in the global shell rail/menu rather than inside the page content frame.
Keep the right content area structurally unified: breadcrumb navigation above, actual business content below.

Do not render `FunctionalWorkspace`'s context bar by default on production pages; the topbar is the page identity layer and content should begin with metrics, compact controls, tables, and inspectors.
Use `ui-skill` first for frontend UI changes, then fall back to `finesse-skill` and `taste-skill`.
Preserve child configuration components during Settings shell migration so real save/test/RBAC/audit flows keep working.
Use `/prototype.html` for no-login visual review and the authenticated app route for real production functionality.
Let the left Settings configuration surface determine desktop row height; absolutely contain the audit panel so long diffs cannot inflate both columns.
